vision: A distributable library of AI coding assistant rules, skills, hooks, and an adversarial verification harness for Cursor and Claude Code. The library must dogfood its own authoring standards — including a rigorous, machine-validated state.json schema — before the library is considered trustworthy.
direction: library/cursor/ is the single source of truth for distributable config. Eval pipeline at 93% (368/394), zero scenarios below 70%. Active initiative: state.json v2 schema — rename features→tasks, fixed status and type enums, schema_version field, backward-compat transition then alias removal. Keep flat tasks array (group by status at read time in hooks/metrics/judge). contract.json uses task_id (feature_id accepted as alias). Status lifecycle unchanged: pending→building→evaluating→verified→committed. Do not introduce ambiguous values like done/doing.

trade_offs.decision: Flat tasks array, not grouped buckets
trade_offs.reasoning: Hooks and agents iterate one list today; grouped buckets duplicate items and drift. harness-context.sh and harness_metrics.py can filter by status at read time.
Five hooks, harness_lint.py, HARNESS_STANDARD.md, and 27 eval scenarios already encode this lifecycle. done conflates verified and committed; doing conflates building and evaluating.

trade_offs.decision: Explicit type enum on every task
trade_offs.alternative: Infer type from id prefix only (feat-/gap-/spike-)
trade_offs.reasoning: Id prefixes are convention not validation; explicit type enables lint enforcement and clearer planner output.
22+ eval scenario seeds and 6 shell hooks read features today; alias prevents eval regression during phased rollout.
Preserves audit trail; metrics exclude cancelled from backlog counts.

trade_offs.alternative: Keep symlinks tracked, gitignore only transient files
trade_offs.reasoning: Matches how consumer projects treat IDE config; library/cursor/ is the distributable artifact
spec.md was read once (plan gate) then became stale. Single file eliminates drift by design.
